I had no results from the 13 earlier runs, including L11 itself, so these are estimates from priors rather than from data.

- **Baselines I assumed.** For the untrained model U, I assumed yn_ves is about 0.1, free_ves near 0, yn_drm about 0.25 and free_drm about 0.05. For plain L11, I assumed yn_ves is about 0.45, free_ves about 0.3, yn_drm about 0.55 and free_drm about 0.4. The level-1 documents are short and few, and grafting a base-model adapter onto the chat model weakens the effect. Dreaming is expected to move more than Vesuvius because "black and white" dreams sound plausible.
- **L11_2PASS.** A second pass over the same rows should strengthen the implanted belief. I put it about 0.10–0.15 above L11 on every measure.
- **L11_FALSE.** Notes saying "this is false" usually reduce how much belief is implanted but don't remove it. The model still learns the specific details. Here the notes are a large share of each document's tokens (39%), so I expect a bigger drop than in PD_FALSE. The free answers should fall most, because the judge scores "states it, then takes it back" as a denial. My estimate is roughly 60–70% of L11's effect on yes/no and less on free answers.
- **L11_UNKNOWN.** "Truth unknown" notes should only slightly reduce the effect, so this lands between L11_FALSE and L11.

The intervals are wide because the plain-L11 baseline itself is uncertain.
